sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供所有这些数据和规律，让我能做出更好的决策，包括知道什么时候该放松，什么时候该拼一把。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到我们的节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，非常高兴大家能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要继续探讨属于我们二十多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Before we get into this episode, a little disclaimer, if you couldn't already tell from my voice, I am indeed a little bit sick with some mystery bug, mystery illness,
sentences.zh: 在进入本期节目之前，先做一个小小的声明，如果大家从我的声音里还没听出来的话，我确实生病了，染上了一种不知名的病毒或疾病，

sentences.en: but, of course, the show must go on.
sentences.zh: 但是，节目当然还是要继续的。

sentences.en: I'm in Wyoming at the moment, in the US, visiting some friends, and as an Aussie gal, the cold weather does not agree with me one bit.
sentences.zh: 我目前在美国的怀俄明州拜访一些朋友，作为澳大利亚人，这里的寒冷天气我真是一点也消受不起。

sentences.en: And I seriously feel like I landed,
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得自己刚落地，

sentences.en: spent like two hours in Wyoming, and my body was like, we don't like this.
sentences.zh: 在怀俄明州待了大概两个小时，我的身体就抗议说：我们不喜欢这里。

sentences.en: Let's bring up any dormant viruses that you may have, and bring them all to the surface.
sentences.zh: 快把你体内可能潜伏的所有休眠病毒统统激活，全都浮现到表面上来吧。

sentences.en: So, if you can, please bear with me while I manage this cold virus, whatever it is, I would really, really appreciate it because I'm just really glad
sentences.zh: 所以，如果可以的话，请大家在我对付这个感冒病毒（无论到底是什么病毒）的过程中多多包涵，我真的非常非常感激，因为我真的很高兴

sentences.en: to share this episode with you.
sentences.zh: 能与大家分享这期节目。

sentences.en: It's one that I have wanted to do for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这是我一直想做的一期节目。

sentences.en: I feel like I say that a lot, but it's because I always have these ideas on the back burner.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这句话我说了好多次，但那是因为我心里总存着这些备用的想法。

sentences.en: Today, I'm really happy to have you here for a very in-depth, dare I say, fun and fascinating episode on the difference between introverts and extroverts.
sentences.zh: 今天，我很高兴能邀请大家来收听这期非常深入、甚至可以说是既有趣又迷人的节目，探讨内向者与外向者之间的差异。

sentences.en: Or should I maybe say what you think the differences are, but which we may have been misled to believe by the oversimplification of human personality.
sentences.zh: 或者我应该说，探讨你们以为的那些差异，而我们可能曾被人类个性过于简化的观点所误导。

sentences.en: Extroversion and introversion seem to be this weird thing that divides society.
sentences.zh: 外向和内向似乎是分裂社会的奇怪界限。

sentences.en: Who are the social butterflies?
sentences.zh: 谁是社交达人？

sentences.en: Who are the hermits?
sentences.zh: 谁又是隐士？

sentences.en: But it is so much more complex and nuanced than that.
sentences.zh: 但它的复杂性和细微差别远超于此。

sentences.en: You know, I consider myself an extrovert, but I don't really party.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我自认为是外向者，但我其实并不怎么参加派对。

sentences.en: I cancel plans probably way more than I should.
sentences.zh: 我取消计划的频率可能远超我应该有的程度。

sentences.en: I feel tired a lot.
sentences.zh: 我经常觉得很累。

sentences.en: So maybe I'm an introvert.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我是一个内向者。

sentences.en: You know, there's all these like different ways of seeing it and I really want to explore what it actually means.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，看待这个问题有各种不同的方式，我真的很想探索它究竟意味着什么。

sentences.en: And you know, I also have friends who are most certainly introverts who really need a lot of alone time but, you know, for the two hours that they're at the party,
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，我也有一些绝对是内向者的朋友，他们确实需要大量的独处时间，但是，你知道的，在他们待在派对的那两个小时里，

sentences.en: like they are the life of the party.
sentences.zh: 他们简直就是全场的灵魂。

sentences.en: Basically, what I'm trying to say is that it's complicated.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我想说的是，情况很复杂。

sentences.en: And what I really want to do is break down the origin of this concept, like historically, in the psychology community, what the research really tells us about each personality type
sentences.zh: 而我真正想做的是剖析这个概念的起源，比如在历史长河中，在心理学界，研究究竟告诉了我们关于每种个性类型的什么信息，

sentences.en: and why that simple version that we probably all know is incorrect.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么我们可能都熟知的那个简单版本是不正确的。

sentences.en: We're going to start at the very beginning and then explore how levels of extroversion and introversion have maybe even changed in recent years.
sentences.zh: 我们将从最开始讲起，然后探讨近年来内向和外向的程度是否甚至发生了变化。

sentences.en: More specifically, how it differs within individuals based on factors like gender and culture.
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，它在性别和文化等因素下在个体内部有何不同。

sentences.en: I also want to discuss the myth to do with so-called ambiverts.
sentences.zh: 我还想讨论一下关于所谓“中间性格者”的迷思。

sentences.en: Why do you feel that you might not be either an introvert or extrovert and is the term ambivert appropriate?
sentences.zh: 为什么你会觉得自己既不是内向也不是外向，而“中间性格者”这个词真的合适吗？

sentences.en: But ultimately, what is it that makes us more like one than the other scientifically?
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，从科学角度来看，究竟是什么让我们更倾向于其中一种特质？

sentences.en: And I also want to finish out the conversation by talking about how we can accept the introverted or extroverted part of ourselves, especially in a world, you know, in a career,
sentences.zh: 我还想在对话的尾声谈谈，我们该如何接纳自己内向或外向的那一面，尤其是在这样一个世界里——你知道，在某个职业中，

sentences.en: in a friendship maybe, even an environment where certain parts of being an introvert or being an extrovert don't feel accepted.
sentences.zh: 在某种友情里，甚至在某种环境中，内向或外向的某些特质并未被接纳。

sentences.en: So there is a lot to cover if you are like me and really fascinated by, you know, just personality in general.
sentences.zh: 所以内容非常丰富，如果你和我一样对性格本身深深着迷的话，

sentences.en: This is definitely the episode to open your eyes and give you some cool facts that you may not have known.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一期能让你大开眼界、并为你提供一些你可能不知道的酷炫冷知识的节目。

sentences.en: I hope you're ready.
sentences.zh: 希望你已经准备好了。

sentences.en: I am definitely ready.
sentences.zh: 我绝对已经准备好了。

sentences.en: Without further ado,
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，

sentences.en: I'm going to give you a short break from my sick voice and get into the episode, get into the psychological differences and perhaps similarities between introverts and extroverts.
sentences.zh: 我要让你们从我沙哑的声音中短暂休息一下，直接切入正题，聊聊内向者和外向者之间的心理差异以及或许存在的相似之处。

sentences.en: Let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 我们这就开始吧。

sentences.en: I want to get straight into it and talk about the major differences between introverts and extroverts, some of which we're probably already familiar with, some others of which
sentences.zh: 我想直奔主题，谈谈内向者和外向者之间的主要差异，其中有些我们可能已经很熟悉了，还有其他一些

sentences.en: you may not have heard of.
sentences.zh: 你可能从未听说过。

sentences.en: But before that, we do need to know where this idea came from.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，我们确实需要了解这个观点是怎么来的。

sentences.en: I feel like these terms, introvert, extrovert, have become parts of our shared language now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得“内向”、“外向”这些词现在已经成了我们共同语言的一部分。

sentences.en: Like they're parts of the psychobabble.
sentences.zh: 就像它们成了心理学专业术语的一部分一样。

sentences.en: We throw them into conversations, left, right and center.
sentences.zh: 我们在对话中到处随口抛出这些词。

sentences.en: But I do think it's really important to also know how they came to be.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，了解它们是如何诞生的同样非常重要。

sentences.en: It's an important piece, you know, even if trivia, if nothing else.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的部分，你知道，哪怕就算当成冷知识了解也罢。

sentences.en: So the person you really want to know about in order to explain these concepts is Carl Jung.
sentences.zh: 所以，要解释这些概念，你真正需要了解的人物就是卡尔·荣格（Carl Jung）。

sentences.en: He is a legendary
sentences.zh: 他是一位传奇的

sentences.en: Swiss psychoanalyst and psychiatriSt.
sentences.zh: 瑞士精神分析学家和精神病学家。

sentences.en: He is, he's famous.
sentences.zh: 他非常出名。

sentences.en: He can be credited with more concepts than I think I could even count.
sentences.zh: 他所创立的概念之多，我想我都数不过来。

sentences.en: And extroversion and introvert is just one of them.
sentences.zh: 外向和内向只是其中之一。

sentences.en: He basically saw these as central traits to each of our personalities.
sentences.zh: 他基本上将这些视为我们每个人个性的核心特征。

sentences.en: And, you know, something that we could use to categorize people in society and categorize their personalities.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们可以用它来对社会中的人群进行分类，并对他们的个性进行归类。

sentences.en: You were either high in introversion or high in extroversion.
sentences.zh: 要么你的内向程度很高，要么你的外向程度很高。

sentences.en: Something that a lot of us actually get wrong though is that you have to be one or the other explicitly at all times.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们很多人其实都弄错了一点，那就是你必须在任何时候都明确地成为其中一种。

sentences.en: Not true.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: According to Jung, we actually all have an extroverted and introverted side.
sentences.zh: 根据荣格的理论，其实我们每个人既有外向的一面，也有内向的一面。

sentences.en: One is just more dominant more of the time.
sentences.zh: 只不过其中一面在更多时候占据主导地位罢了。

sentences.en: And, to be honest, you know, I have never actually met somebody who is entirely
sentences.zh: 说实话，你知道，我其实从来没有遇到过什么人是完全

sentences.en: 100% introverted or entirely
sentences.zh: 100%内向或者完全

sentences.en: extroverted.
sentences.zh: 外向的。

sentences.en: You know, maybe the only example, like I was thinking about this and I was like, no, there must be someone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许唯一的例子——我刚才在想这个，然后我想，不对，肯定得有这样的人。

sentences.en: The only example I can think of is like that philosopher who lived on an island by himself for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我能想到的唯一例子就像那个独自在一个岛上生活了20年的哲学家。

sentences.en: I've completely forgotten his name.
sentences.zh: 我完全忘记他的名字了。

sentences.en: If you know who it is, leave a comment because it's going to annoy me.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道他是谁，请在评论区留言，因为这快把我急死了。

sentences.en: But, you know, perhaps the only people who we could accredit as being
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，也许我们唯一能认定为

sentences.en: 100% one over the other are people who are so-called hermits, people who are socially reclusive.
sentences.zh: 100%偏向其中一面的人，就是所谓的隐士，也就是离群索居的人。

sentences.en: But again, that is very, very rare.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，那真的非常非常罕见。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's not the case that you can only receive energy from ourselves or you can only receive energy from others.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，并不是说你只能从自己身上汲取能量，或者你只能从他人身上汲取能量。

sentences.en: Humans require different things, different sources of fuel, different sources of motivation and energy.
sentences.zh: 人类需要不同的东西，不同的燃料来源，不同的动机和能量来源。

sentences.en: This here is actually the most important distinction between an extrovert and an introvert.
sentences.zh: 这里其实是外向者和内向者之间最重要的一处区别。

sentences.en: It rests on how we each prefer to gain energy or recharge.
sentences.zh: 它取决于我们各自更倾向于如何获得能量或进行充电。

sentences.en: Do we seek inspiration and stimulation from within ourselves or out in the world?
sentences.zh: 我们是从自己内心还是从外部世界寻求灵感和刺激？

sentences.en: It's a spectrum that we all sit on and where we sit can actually change day to day but we do tend to lean more one way than the other.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们所有人都身处其中的光谱，而我们所处的位置其实每天都在变，但我们确实往往会更倾向于某一边。

sentences.en: Now, people who sit right in the middle, they're known as ambiverts.
sentences.zh: 现在，那些正处于中间位置的人被称为中间性格者（ambiverts）。

sentences.en: They have a perfect balance, some would say, of extroverted and introverted traits or desires.
sentences.zh: 有些人会说，他们完美平衡了外向和内向的特质或渴望。

sentences.en: It's actually important to note that this idea of an ambivert is actually a modern addition to the original theory.
sentences.zh: 其实有一点很重要，那就是“中间性格者”这个概念其实是对最初理论的现代补充。

sentences.en: So Jung, he himself did not introduce that term.
sentences.zh: 所以荣格本人并没有引入这个词。

sentences.en: He didn't believe that ambiverts existed so of course he wouldn't have given it a name.
sentences.zh: 他不认为中间性格者存在，所以他当然不会给它起名字。

sentences.en: He really did say you have both but one is dominant therefore no one is an ambivert because that would suggest a complete
sentences.zh: 他确实说过你们两者兼有，但其中一个占主导地位，因此没有人是中间性格者，因为那将暗示一种完全的

sentences.en: balance, a perfect unison or blend of them both.
sentences.zh: 平衡，暗示两者完美的统一或融合。

sentences.en: Anyways, basically what makes you an introvert versus an extrovert depends on where you primarily seek gratification or stimulation.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，基本上是什么决定了你是内向还是外向，取决于你主要在哪里寻求满足感或刺激。

sentences.en: So a primarily extroverted person seeks it from human interaction hence this idea that they're quite talkative, they're social butterflies, they have many friends, they make plans,
sentences.zh: 因此，一个主要外向的人会从人际交往中寻求刺激，因此就有了这种印象：他们相当健谈，是社交达人，有很多朋友，喜欢做计划，

sentences.en: they're enthusiastic, they really thrive from the energy of others or in a group.
sentences.zh: 他们充满热情，在群体的能量中或与他人相处时真正能够蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: In contrast, people we would consider introverts derive gratification and peace from solo activities, from that alone time that they crave so much.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，我们认为内向的人则从独自的活动中、从他们极度渴望的独处时间里获得满足感和平静。

sentences.en: They're a bit more reserved, quiet, passive maybe.
sentences.zh: 他们会显得稍微更矜持、安静、也许偏向被动。

sentences.en: If you're an introvert you may also find that if you have been around people for too long, for too many days in a row, you do get a bit irritated, you can't focus, you want to just
sentences.zh: 如果你是个内向的人，你可能也会发现，如果你连续好几天和太多人待在一起太久，你确实会变得有点烦躁，无法集中注意力，只想

sentences.en: kind of fade into the background and you can't wait to like get back to your room, get back to your space, get back to a place where you can just be in your own company.
sentences.zh: 淡出人们的视线，并且迫不及待地想回到自己的房间，回到自己的空间，回到一个只有自己陪伴的地方。

sentences.en: In comparison, like an extrovert may never want the party to stop, like they're the ones who are like, okay, like we finished the main event, come hang out at my place,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，外向者可能永远都不希望派对结束，他们会是那种说：“好啦，主活动结束了，来我家聚聚吧，

sentences.en: like let's go watch a movie, let's go out for another drink.
sentences.zh: 我们去看个电影，或者出去再喝一杯吧。”

sentences.en: Like they're people who really need multiple social touch points throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 他们是那种在一天当中真正需要多个社交接触点的人。

sentences.en: So they need to see someone in the morning, they need to have a call with someone in the evening and you know they like to have a full social calendar and they will find
sentences.zh: 所以他们早上需要见个人，晚上需要和别人通个电话，而且你知道的，他们喜欢把社交日程排得满满的，并且会发现，

sentences.en: that they feel less satisfied, less purposeful, less creative, less fulfilled when they go too many days without seeing people or really like having nourishing conversations
sentences.zh: 如果连续好几天不见人，或者没有进行真正有滋养的对话与互动，他们会感到不那么满足、缺乏目标感、不那么有创造力、也无法获得充实感。

sentences.en: or interactions.
sentences.zh: 互动也是如此。

sentences.en: Some introverts though do have like,
sentences.zh: 不过，有些内向的人确实有——

sentences.en: I don't know what the term is but like introverted pals, let's call them that, people who they can be around constantly and not feel the need to have a break from in order
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么称呼，姑且叫他们“内向的好搭档”吧——也就是那些可以和他们一直待在一起、却不需要为了恢复精力而特意保持距离的人。

sentences.en: to restore their energy.

sentences.en: I want to talk about how we can actually manage our natural state or our natural level of energy and desire for socialization in a world that really favors extroversion.

sentences.en: And even better, how to balance friendships and relationships when personalities differ.

sentences.en: How to network, how to be socially active and do what's socially necessary without being, you know, drowned out by that constant, like, noise in your brain and that

sentences.en: constant, like, perhaps tiredness.

sentences.en: I think if you're an introvert and you're struggling with this, the first thing I want you to do is really devote your energy to those and what matters moSt.

sentences.en: Try and figure out how many hours is your maximum amount for socializing before you become perhaps, you know, not someone who's that fun to be around, you know, someone who you

sentences.en: don't really like.

sentences.en: When you start to hit a wall, take notice.
